text: Swimming encompasses several essential skills, one of which is the use of goggles. Goggles are worn by swimmers to shield their eyes from water and prevent entry. They are typically made of lightweight, flexible materials designed to fit snugly over the swimmer's head. Goggles can prevent eye irritation or injury from water and reduce drag, thereby improving performance in the water. Another crucial skill in swimming is the ability to perform laps, which entails swimming a specific distance or time. Laps can be performed in various swimming strokes, including freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke, and butterfly, and can be practiced both in the water and on a poolside lane. Through practice and dedication, anyone can master the art of swimming and perform laps effectively.
